title: Place value: × 10 and ÷ 10
keyIdea: Each place is worth ten times the place to its right, so × 10 moves every digit one place left and ÷ 10 moves it one place right.

kid: Each place is worth ten times the place on its right. A ten is ten ones. A one is ten tenths.
When you multiply by 10, every digit moves one place to the left. When you divide by 10, every digit moves one place to the right. The decimal point stays still. A zero holds an empty place.
adult: Apples cost £0.35 each, so a crate of 10 costs £3.50 and a pallet of 100 costs £35. Multiplying by 10 moves every digit one place left; the decimal point does not move.
× 10 shifts each digit one column left: 4.7 × 10 = 47 and 4.7 × 100 = 470, with a zero as a placeholder. ÷ 10 shifts right: 47 ÷ 10 = 4.7 and 3 ÷ 100 = 0.03.
'Add a zero' fails for decimals: 4.7 × 10 is not 4.70. 'The digits move and the point stays' always works.

familyTip: Write a number on paper strips, one digit per square, under a fixed decimal point. Slide the strip to multiply or divide by 10.

pool.prompt: A digit moves from the tens place to the hundreds place. What happened?
pool.explain: One place left means ten times as much.

pool.prompt: A digit in the hundreds place is worth how many times the same digit in the tens place?
pool.explain: Each place is worth 10 times the one to its right.

pool.prompt: Sam says 4.7 × 10 = 4.70 because “× 10 adds a zero”. What is the right answer?
pool.hint: Does 4.70 have a different value from 4.7?
pool.explain: 4.70 is the same number as 4.7. × 10 moves each digit one place left: 47.

visual.caption: Press × 10 or ÷ 10 and watch the digits slide. The decimal point stays put.
